answer.candidate_RAM: Use the original single guest managed physical envelope as a conservative candidate, not all chosen DRAM. Source and this saved boot establish its high end is preserved from original BootArgs and is below the recorded MCC/VRAM exclusions. All109 current guest pmap-io and37 physical device-segment records are disjoint. This is useful positive evidence for that narrower interval, not authority to map all physical memory.
answer.not_deliberate_new_cap: HV.load_raw computes guest mem_size=original phys_base+original mem_size-new phys_base. The continuing wrapper checks only its payload reservation against MCC and does not reduce the entire guest envelope by min(MCC,VRAM,other exclusions). No maxmem option is present. Thus the inherited high happens to be conservative for the observed sources; there is no existing complete native policy producer.
answer.remaining_blocker: Native configure still needs a trusted same-boot bounded platform policy handoff for the selected envelope and retained boot allocations, with declared exclusion-source coverage. Three MCC ranges are finite four-TZ-class evidence, not global device-exclusion completeness. No code or metadata complete=1 claim is supplied.

settled_source_facts.fact: XNU distinguishes actual chosen dram-base/size from kernel-managed gPhysBase/Size; chosen physical DRAM bounds do not remove holes or prove DMA eligibility.
gPhysBase comes from guest BootArgs; gPhysSize/mem_size is page-rounded memSize and may be limited further by memory_size. These define VM management bounds, not an exclusion inventory.
pa_valid is only vm_first_phys<=PA<vm_last_phys; pmap_valid_page delegates to it and source TODO explicitly mentions physical holes. No public/KPI completeness oracle follows.

/defaults pmap-io-ranges is an array of24-byte addr/len/wimg/signature records; CARVEOUT is bit30 and NOT_IO bit27. Records describe I/O/decorated physical ranges, not a promised exhaustive MCC/device reservation census. New reader must reject partial records rather than adopt source division truncation.

Pinned T8103 profile reads four TZ slots, assumes common MCC/plane configuration, skips enabled bad-bound slots with a warning, and emits a sentinel list. DT fallback region-id-2/4 applies when its register profile is absent. A valid bounded list alone is not proof all device reservations are represented.

Bounded host reads retain the raw MCC list and compare it before guest writes. Entire guest high remains original high; the wrapper relocates ADT/TrustCache/RAMDisk through topOfKernelData. That boot/payload interval remains excluded from new owned backing even when some pages are later freed.

private_saved_metadata_check.scope: Read existing local saved bytes only. No hardware/log acquisition or old grade changed. Raw addresses, property data and device identifiers are not copied here; only source-bound hashes/keys/counts/predicates.
limits: Full guest BootArgs bytes were not separately captured; its envelope is derived from exact original BootArgs+before-start layout+unchanged captured HV/launcher transformation.
Device remap numeric nonintersections are conservative comparisons, not an assertion of remap address-space semantics.
Known disjointness does not infer completeness of any missing/unknown DT exclusion class. Original PCIe failed7/10 grade and STOP remain unchanged.

minimum_trusted_policy_inputs: Immutable same-boot owner/domain identity and source-bound board/SoC/address profile; hashes of exact KC, ramdisk, launcher/HV and incoming guest ADT. These are provenance, not cryptographic authentication of arbitrary caller metadata.

Exact original guest envelope boundaries, preserved as one source interval rather than broadened to chosen DRAM or merged with neighboring RAM. Cross-check original BootArgs ABI/revision/length with pinned writer, chosen64-bit dram bounds, final guest layout and runtime page size16KiB/PA36bit. Do not infer DRAM base by masking a pointer for a generic platform.

All four T8103 TZ slot classifications/validation status or an equivalently trusted exact same-boot exclusion-set source, actual bounded sentinel/cardinality and unchanged-before-launch comparison. Empty/partial/invalid enabled-slot information is not absence. Do not label four-TZ coverage global MCC/device completeness.

Whole framebuffer allocation extent from boot video/known geometry; all known DT pmap-io/device firmware physical spans that may intersect the chosen envelope; explicit scope/provenance for every omitted class. Unknown/unsupported/missing required encoding is a refusal, not permission.

Guest-owned retained boot reservation through topOfKernelData, exact BootArgs/ADT/TrustCache/ramdisk allocations and other live handoff allocations. Conservative coarser reserved cover is permissible only explicitly documented; it must never free gaps or erase original source provenance.

Actual control-protection helper augments this base policy with its same-setup control physical pages. Native backing validation separately excludes root/leaf/data aliases and other live owners. Base policy is not a substitute for allocation identity/preparation, control protection or same-owner conflict checks.

future_guest_copy_only_handoff.scope: A separately reviewed isolated host ADT metadata helper is a possible next source-only implementation. It changes only the guest ADT copy and consumes existing bounded collection inputs; no m1n1 runtime/source change, new read, boot or native configure is authorized here.
future_guest_copy_only_handoff.payload: Fixed version/size/board profile, same-boot nonce/setup binding, exact KC+ramdisk hashes, source-envelope and page-granule fields, original RAM intervals, exclusion source counts/digests/coverage labels, exact nonoverlapping reservation union and derivation status/reason. Keep all raw source ranges privately bound; guest receives only bounded policy metadata necessary for validation. No user-controlled complete flag can manufacture provenance.
future_guest_copy_only_handoff.ADT_hash_cycle: Embedding final full ADT SHA inside that same ADT is self-referential. Embed a precisely defined incoming/base-ADT digest excluding the new policy property; retain final serialized guest-ADT SHA in the external candidate/capture receipt and verify dump-back. Guest-side consistency must bind actual chosen/BootArgs/envelope and the canonical excluded-property digest; hashes do not authenticate an untrusted host.
future_guest_copy_only_handoff.pipeline: Validate metadata/profile/cardinalities and all source coverage before control pin/configure. Recompute known interval disjointness and exact union; bind to same setup through the existing internal native/control path, not a detached arbitrary receipt. Reject stale packet hash, changed ADT/layout/envelope/exclusions or unsupported source status. Do not replay this historical saved policy on a future boot.

interval_and_capacity_guards: All ranges nonempty, overflow-free and below2^36; candidate full16KiB page must fit wholly inside ONE original RAM interval, not an adjacent union. Original RAM intervals/boundaries retained exactly; no first-eight selection or invented expansion.

Preserve exact source exclusion intervals and their evidence. For a relevant range which intersects RAM, retain its full boundary (round reserved coverage outward to16KiB only with explicit derived-vs-original records), never clip a hazard inward. Disjoint exclusions may be scoped out only by checked disjointness from every original RAM interval with a retained audit reason, never merely to meet capacity.

Overlapping/adjacent reserved intervals may be represented by their exact set union with source membership retained, since c585 requires nonoverlap. Refuse if the exact union exceeds8, if original RAM count exceeds8, or if control-helper final union exceeds8. Never truncate, drop a range or substitute a bounding interval as an unrecorded capacity trick.

If a conservative boot reservation overlaps a freshly pinned control page, frozen control002 must refuse; do not punch that page out to force success or retry the uncertain/pinned lifecycle. All allocator/preparation/ref-retention rules remain intact.
